A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 22 readable pages including Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments comparing strategic, adversarial, and clean training on CIFAR-10, GTSRB, and CIFAR-100, plus additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the main evaluations and all seven experimental subsections of Appendix C.

M1.justification: The strategic training objectives and optimization procedures in Section 5 are identical. The preference-attack adaptation, utility-inference procedures, and sequential attack variants in Appendix C are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, GTSRB, and CIFAR-100 under the same opponent scenarios, including k-hot, semantic, anti-semantic, preference-order, and continuous-utility settings.

E2.justification: The clean and adversarial training baselines participate in the same comparisons. Appendix C.7 also retains the same weighted-target, sequential, sequential-adversarial, and multi-targeted comparison methods.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings in Sections 4 and 6 and Appendices B–C are identical, including data splits, architectures, metrics, training budgets, and attack procedures. Appendix B.3 retains the 8/255 threat budget and seven training versus twenty evaluation PGD steps.

E4.justification: Both retain the same analyses of attack semantics, incentive misspecification, risk mitigation, all-knowing adversaries, utility inference, and utility-order alignment. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is identical, including standard errors in Table 3, variability displays in Figures 7 and 9, and the ten random preference-order instances with mean and standard deviation reporting in Appendix C.4.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and findings match throughout Tables 1–8, the experimental figures, and accompanying passages. Appendix results, including utility recovery and continuous-utility comparisons, are retained without changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, inequalities, and derivations are unchanged, including Equations (1)–(13) and the continuous-utility reasoning in Appendix C.7.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions: modeling opponent incentives, training against incentive uncertainty sets, and balancing strategic robustness with clean accuracy.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic structure and strategic gains are identical. Section 6.2 and Appendix A retain the same qualifications about incentive misspecification, uncertainty-set-dependent protection, and deployment limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical preprocessing, hyperparameters, batch-size exceptions, hardware, and runtime information. Code links and code/checkpoint availability statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography contain the same cited works and research positioning, including the claimed connection between multiclass strategic classification and adversarial learning.

P1.justification: v3 adds the running text 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body wording, terminology, section organization, and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The publication header appears throughout v3. Figures 1 and 2 and surrounding text shift slightly on page 2, with minor paragraph reflow; figure contents, captions, table structures, and the remaining body layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the complete scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations of v2, including its appendices. The publication header, updated arXiv stamp, and small page-2 layout adjustments establish no meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
